gold.name: Gold
gold.importParity: MCX Gold = (COMEX $/troy oz ÷ 31.1035) × 10 × USD/INR × 1.12 (6% BCD + 3% AIDC + 3% GST, post-July 2024 budget)
gold.supplyControl: No single entity controls gold supply. Top producers: China 11%, Russia 10%, Australia 10%, Canada 5%. Central banks are the dominant holders.
demandDrivers: Central bank reserve accumulation (China, Russia, India RBI buying since 2022)
Indian jewellery (25% of global demand — wedding season Oct–Feb peaks)
Gold ETFs (institutional investment flow)
Electronics and semiconductors (industrial)
Safe-haven demand during geopolitical or financial stress
priceDrivers: USD strength — gold and dollar move inversely
US real yields (10Y TIPS) — higher real rates raise opportunity cost of holding gold
Central bank buying — especially EM central banks diversifying away from USD
Geopolitical risk — war, sanctions, banking crises lift gold
India import duty — government can change duty; each 1% duty change shifts MCX price ~₹1,000/10g
Indian rupee — a weaker INR amplifies MCX gold price even when COMEX is flat
gold.keyRisk: MCX-COMEX spread can widen when Indian import duty changes or USD/INR moves sharply — watch basis risk.
gold.taxNote: Gold ETF LTCG: 12.5% after 12 months (Budget 2024). Physical gold LTCG: 12.5% without indexation after 2 years. MCX futures gains: non-speculative business income at slab rate. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

silver.name: Silver
silver.supplyControl: Top producers: Mexico 22%, Peru 14%, China 13%, Russia 7%. Unlike gold, 70% of silver supply comes as a by-product of mining other metals (copper, zinc, lead) — supply is inelastic.
demandDrivers: Industrial use (60% of demand) — solar panels, EVs, electronics, 5G
Jewellery and silverware (India is world's largest silver importer for this)
Investment demand — silver ETFs, bars and coins
Green energy transition — each solar panel uses ~20g of silver; global solar buildout is a structural demand tailwind
priceDrivers: Gold-silver ratio — historically 60–80x; when ratio spikes above 80, silver is cheap relative to gold
Industrial cycle — silver tracks copper in risk-on/risk-off regimes more than gold does
Solar capacity additions — China solar policy directly affects silver industrial demand
USD strength (inverse)
India import duty and monsoon (agri income → silver buying in rural India)
silver.keyRisk: Silver is far more volatile than gold — easily swings 3–5% in a session. High lot value (₹30L per lot) amplifies P&L. Silver Mini (5 kg) is available for smaller capital.
silver.taxNote: Same as gold futures — gains taxed as business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

crude.name: Crude Oil
crude.importParity: MCX Crude = WTI ($/bbl) × USD/INR × 1.025 (includes import duty differential)
crude.supplyControl: OPEC+ (12 OPEC members + Russia + allied non-OPEC producers — Angola exited Jan 2024) controls ~40% of global oil supply and sets production quotas quarterly. Saudi Arabia is the swing producer — can flood or restrict supply unilaterally within limits. US shale (Permian Basin) is the marginal supplier that caps upside.
demandDrivers: Transportation — aviation, shipping, road fuel (60% of global oil demand)
Petrochemicals — plastics, fertilisers
Chinese industrial activity — China alone is 15% of global demand
Indian fuel demand — India is world's 3rd largest oil consumer
Seasonal driving demand (US summer, India winter)
priceDrivers: OPEC+ production decisions — each 1 mbpd cut historically lifts WTI $5–10/bbl
US EIA weekly inventory data (Wednesday 8 PM IST) — draw = bullish, build = bearish
US shale rig count (Baker Hughes, Friday) — higher rigs = more future supply = price cap
China PMI and import data — weak China demand is the biggest bearish driver
Middle East geopolitics — Strait of Hormuz tension (20% of global oil transits through it)
USD strength — oil is priced in dollars; strong USD = lower oil for non-US buyers
Seasonal: US driving season (Memorial Day–Labor Day) lifts gasoline/crude
crude.keyRisk: Crude is the most geopolitically sensitive commodity. Weekend OPEC+ surprises and Middle East flare-ups cause gap opens on Monday. Retail traders should avoid holding large overnight positions before OPEC+ meetings.
crude.taxNote: MCX crude futures gains: non-speculative business income. CTT 0.01% on sell. Petrol/diesel prices in India are state-controlled and do not move with MCX crude in real time.

copper.name: Copper
copper.supplyControl: Chile (25%) and Peru (11%) together control 36% of global mined copper supply. Congo (DRC) is rising fast. The Democratic Republic of Congo + Zambia control 70% of global cobalt (copper by-product). China controls 40% of global copper smelting/refining capacity — a chokepoint even when mines are elsewhere.
demandDrivers: China construction and infrastructure (accounts for ~55% of global copper demand)
Electric vehicles — each EV uses 83kg of copper vs 22kg in ICE cars
Power grid buildout — renewable energy and grid upgrades are copper-intensive
AI data centres — each hyperscale data centre uses thousands of tonnes of copper wiring
Indian infrastructure (roads, rail, power) — growing demand centre
priceDrivers: China economic data — PMI, property sector health, stimulus announcements
LME warehouse stock levels — low inventory signals supply tightness
Mine supply disruptions — strikes in Chile/Peru (frequent), floods, political instability
AI and energy transition narrative — long-term structural demand story
USD strength (inverse — copper priced in dollars on LME/COMEX)
COMEX-LME basis — arbitrage between US and London markets creates price signals
copper.keyRisk: Copper's large lot size (2,500 kg, ~₹24L contract value) makes it high-capital. LME price is the global benchmark; COMEX is the US proxy. MCX follows COMEX with import duty overlay. Copper is called 'Dr. Copper' because it has the best track record of predicting global economic direction.
copper.taxNote: MCX copper futures: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

zinc.name: Zinc
zinc.importParity: MCX Zinc = LME Zinc ($/tonne) ÷ 1000 × USD/INR × 1.068 (Basic Customs Duty 5% + IGST ~18%)
zinc.supplyControl: China mines 31% and refines 44% of global zinc. Peru (11%) and Australia (10%) are the next largest miners. India's Hindustan Zinc (Vedanta subsidiary) is among the world's top five zinc-lead miners and supplies roughly 75% of India's primary zinc needs — making it the single most important stock to watch for MCX zinc price direction.
keyBodies: International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG)
demandDrivers: Galvanizing (55% of global demand) — zinc-coated steel prevents rust in construction, auto bodies, white goods
Die-casting alloys for automobile parts, hardware, and electronics enclosures
Brass production (copper-zinc alloy) — plumbing, electrical fittings, decorative hardware
Indian infrastructure — galvanized steel pipes, power transmission towers, railway wagons
Battery sector — zinc-air and zinc-ion batteries as next-generation storage alternatives
priceDrivers: LME zinc inventory — low stocks signal supply tightness and push spot premium higher
China galvanized steel demand — real estate and auto sector health are the leading indicators
Hindustan Zinc production guidance — output cuts or smelter maintenance directly affects Indian supply
Energy costs for smelting — zinc smelting is electricity-intensive; European energy crisis caused smelter closures in 2022
USD/INR — MCX zinc tracks LME via import parity; rupee depreciation raises MCX price
zinc.keyRisk: Zinc is closely tied to the steel and construction cycle. A China property sector slowdown is the dominant bearish risk — it hit zinc prices hard in 2022–2024. Hindustan Zinc results and Vedanta group debt restructuring news are India-specific volatility triggers.
zinc.taxNote: MCX zinc futures gains: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

aluminium.name: Aluminium
aluminium.importParity: MCX Aluminium = LME Aluminium ($/tonne) ÷ 1000 × USD/INR × 1.068 (BCD 7.5% + IGST)
aluminium.supplyControl: China produces 58% of global primary aluminium — the highest concentration of any major metal. Russia (Rusal, 6%) and Canada (5%) are the next largest. Aluminium smelting is extremely electricity-intensive (15,000 kWh per tonne), so cheap hydropower nations (China, Russia, Iceland, Norway) dominate. Power costs determine who runs and who shuts.
demandDrivers: Transportation (30% of demand) — aviation, auto (lightweighting for EVs), rail
Construction — windows, facades, roofing, power transmission cables
Packaging — aluminium cans, foil, food-grade containers
Electrical — power cables (aluminium is the main conductor for high-voltage lines)
Green energy transition — EV battery casings, solar panel frames, wind turbine parts
priceDrivers: China smelter output — Chinese aluminium production data (monthly) is the single most important supply signal
Energy prices — European gas/electricity costs determine European smelter viability
LME aluminium warehouse stocks — low inventory = tight physical market
China stimulus — infrastructure and EV policy announcements directly lift aluminium
US tariffs on aluminium imports — Section 232 tariffs distort global trade flows
USD/INR — import parity transmission to MCX
aluminium.keyRisk: Aluminium's price is heavily state-influenced — Chinese government subsidies to aluminium smelters (cheap power, cheap alumina) suppress the global price floor. Sudden US or EU import tariff changes cause sharp basis dislocations. Indian producers (Hindalco, Vedanta's BALCO) are large enough to influence MCX premiums.
aluminium.taxNote: MCX aluminium futures gains: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

lead.name: Lead
lead.importParity: MCX Lead = LME Lead ($/tonne) ÷ 1000 × USD/INR × 1.068 (BCD 5% + IGST)
lead.supplyControl: China dominates global lead smelting (45% of refined output). Australia (14%) and Peru (8%) are the top miners. India's Hindustan Zinc is also a major lead producer — lead is mined alongside zinc at Hindustan Zinc's Rajasthan operations. Secondary (recycled) lead from scrap batteries accounts for 60% of global supply — the auto scrappage cycle is critical.
keyBodies: International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG)
demandDrivers: Lead-acid batteries (80% of demand) — automotive starter batteries, inverter/UPS batteries, e-rickshaws
India specifically: massive inverter and e-rickshaw market keeps Indian lead demand structurally elevated
Industrial batteries — forklifts, telecom backup, grid energy storage
Ammunition and radiation shielding (niche industrial use)
Cable sheathing — declining but still present in legacy power infrastructure
priceDrivers: Auto production and sales — vehicle output directly drives demand for starter batteries
India inverter/UPS battery replacement cycle — 3–4 year battery lifespan creates a steady demand pulse
Scrap lead availability — secondary lead supply depends on old battery collection and smelting capacity
Hindustan Zinc production guidance — lead output from Rajasthan mines affects domestic supply
LME lead inventory — warehouse stocks signal global supply balance
USD/INR — import parity transmission
lead.keyRisk: Lead is the most 'India-driven' base metal on MCX because India's inverter and e-rickshaw market creates unique domestic demand patterns that can diverge from LME. Environmental regulations on secondary lead smelters (informal sector) periodically tighten supply sharply. Lead is also the most prone to seasonal moves — pre-monsoon UPS battery restocking lifts Indian prices.
lead.taxNote: MCX lead futures gains: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

nickel.name: Nickel
nickel.importParity: MCX Nickel = LME Nickel ($/tonne) ÷ 1000 × USD/INR × 1.068 (BCD 5% + IGST ~18%)
nickel.supplyControl: Indonesia banned nickel ore exports in 2020 and now controls the fastest-growing nickel supply chain. Indonesia (48%) and Philippines (12%) dominate mined supply. Russia's Norilsk Nickel (Nornickel) produces ~7% of global nickel and ~35% of high-purity Class 1 nickel used for stainless steel and EV batteries. Indonesia's HPAL (High Pressure Acid Leach) plants supply battery-grade nickel for EV manufacturers directly.
demandDrivers: Stainless steel (70% of global nickel demand) — stainless steel uses 8–12% nickel content
EV batteries — lithium-nickel-manganese-cobalt oxide (NMC) cathode requires 40–80 kg nickel per EV
Superalloys for jet engines and gas turbines (high-temperature applications)
Electroplating — decorative and corrosion-resistant coatings
Indian stainless steel production — India is a major stainless steel producer and growing EV market
priceDrivers: Indonesia export policy — any change to the nickel ore export ban sends shockwaves through the market
EV battery demand trajectory — NMC vs LFP battery chemistry shifts alter nickel demand forecasts sharply
LME nickel warehouse stocks — historically low stocks caused the infamous March 2022 LME short squeeze (price doubled to $100,000/tonne in 2 days)
China stainless steel production — China makes 55% of global stainless steel
Russia sanctions — Norilsk Nickel supply risk from geopolitical escalation
USD/INR — import parity transmission to MCX
nickel.keyRisk: Nickel is the most volatile and 'story-driven' base metal. The 2022 LME short squeeze (price doubled in 48 hours, LME suspended trading) remains the single worst day in exchange history for a commodity. Indonesia policy risk is ever-present. MCX nickel's small lot size (250 kg) makes it accessible but leverage is still high. Battery chemistry shifts (from NMC to LFP) could structurally reduce nickel demand from EVs.
nickel.taxNote: MCX nickel futures gains: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.

natgas.name: Natural Gas
natgas.importParity: MCX NatGas = Henry Hub ($/mmBtu) × USD/INR. Indian LNG import prices track JCC (Japan Crude Cocktail) and long-term contracts — not Henry Hub directly.
natgas.supplyControl: Russia was Europe's dominant gas supplier (pre-2022); now LNG from US, Qatar, Australia fills the gap. The US is the world's largest natural gas producer. Qatar controls ~25% of global LNG trade. Russia's Gazprom still controls the pipelines to much of Eastern Europe. Australia is Asia's largest LNG exporter.
demandDrivers: Power generation — natural gas is the marginal fuel for electricity in the US and increasingly India
Winter heating demand (Northern Hemisphere — Nov–Feb is the peak demand season)
Industrial feedstock — fertiliser production (gas is the key input for urea)
LNG exports from US — high US export demand tightens domestic supply
AI data centre power — gas-fired power plants are being restarted in the US to power AI data centres
priceDrivers: US weather forecasts (3–7 day) — cold snaps drive heating demand and spike prices overnight
EIA Weekly Storage Report (Thursday, 8 PM IST) — draw vs injection vs 5-year average
Hurricane season (June–November) — Gulf of Mexico production disruptions
European LNG import demand — post-Russia sanctions, Europe competes with Asia for LNG cargoes
Henry Hub (US benchmark) — MCX NatGas follows Henry Hub via import parity
AI data centre electricity demand — structural new demand source from 2024 onward
natgas.keyRisk: Natural gas is the most volatile commodity on MCX — daily moves of 5–10% are common. Prices swing on a single weather forecast update. Low margin (₹20–30K) amplifies leverage massively relative to capital. MCX NatGas tracks Henry Hub, not Indian city gas prices.
natgas.taxNote: MCX NatGas futures: business income. CTT 0.01% on sell side.
